info.educationalGoals:
• Set up an embedded development environment.
  • Cross-compile and cross-debug.
  • Explain how an embedded Linux system boots and is built.
  • Read simple circuits and work safely with hardware.
  • Interface with common hardware peripherals from Linux user space.
  • Work from a datasheet.
  • Design modular C programs with a hardware abstraction layer.
  • Write correct concurrent programs.
  • Reason about timing, latency, and determinism.
  • Build a medium-sized embedded application.
  • Find defects and evaluate reliability.
  • Plan and deliver a team project.
  • Demonstrate independent learning.
  • Explain technical work.
  • Develop embedded applications using AI.
info.description: The basics of embedded system organization, hardware-software co-design, and programmable chip technologies are studied. Formal models and specification languages for capturing and analyzing the behaviour of embedded systems. The design and use of tools for system partitioning and hardware/software co-design implementation, validation, and verification are also studied.
info.title: Embedded Systems

info.courseDetails:
You will gain hands-on experience developing embedded applications on your own 32-bit single board computer (BeagleY-AI and custom hardware). You will purchase this hardware through the school during the first week of class instead of buying a required textbook (at similar in cost to a textbook). By the end of the course, you will be able to setup and use a Linux build environment to develop embedded Linux applications. You will have learned to control a wide range of peripherals, wire very simple circuits, and interface a bare-metal (no OS) program with a Linux application. You will have demonstrated a mastery of embedded development on the course group project by implementing a stand-alone product or by interfacing with a larger system. The assignments and project require a significant amount of time to complete. Expect to spend more time on this course than a less hands-on course.

A policy on the use of generative AI tools will be discussed during the first lecture. It is likely that quizzes will be used to assess student learning from assignments in addition to marking submitted assignments.

Lecture attendance is expected and may be incentivized. Lectures will be recorded and quizzes announced ahead of time.
